notes.title: Demons Battling Demons – The Carnival of Company is Live!
notes.content:
Hello, demons battling demons!
Our tiny (but mighty!) two-person team poured our hearts  into The Carnival of Company. Inside our mysterious carnival, you’ll find curious characters, hidden oddities, and maybe even a few surprises that’ll make you laugh—or at least smile.
We’re not some big studio, just two folks who love creating weird worlds. If you give it a try, let us know what you think. Your feedback means everything to us!

Thanks for stopping by, and have fun exploring the Carnival!

notes.title: Demons battling demons!
notes.content:
Hello, demons battling demons,

The release of the game is just around the corner.
We've been working on it for over three years and have learned so much along the way.
We hope we've created a game that will make players happy.
In the intro of Baldur's Gate 1, there was a quote from Nietzsche, and it was very impactful.
Now, we're telling the story of our battle against bosses who commit various sins, and even years later, we still draw inspiration from that quote.
If you have any suggestions, don't hesitate to write.

Best regards
Abil

notes.title: News
notes.content:
Demons vs. Demons!

We're still running tests, and now we have a unique opportunity to focus more on the story.

The story kicks off with Jack, a successful engineer who gets betrayed by Angela, a board member at his company, and ends up cast into hell. From there, he faces demons—both literal and figurative—in an unforgiving underworld. And yeah, there's a big twist coming, but we're not spoiling it here.

One important note: this story isn't an allegory for office life. A lot of people might think that when they first hear it, but what we're really telling is a modern tragedy—a journey with no escape, where those who witness it will hopefully feel some kind of emotional release. That is, if any of us are still capable of catharsis these days.

Stay tuned for more updates, and don't forget to add us to your wishlist!

notes.title: Minor Patch Update
notes.content:
Demons battling demons!

The new minor patch is ready!


 Spain localization has been added to the game.


 Fixed a bug where remapping controls did not save correctly.


 A new tutorial has been added to help players understand the game mechanics better and to provide a clearer explanation of the Path of Carnival (PoC) system.


 Special attack is now non-interruptible to improve combat flow.


 The duration of the parry bonus has been extended for better gameplay balance.


 A timer is now visible when transforming into a demon after eating a brain, providing better visual feedback.


 Various UI adjustments have been made to improve the user experience.

notes.title: Major Update!
notes.content:
Demons battling demons!

The new major patch is ready!
After a lot of hard work, we've made many changes:


 Added German, French, and Italian languages.


 Made changes to the UI style.


 Added key mapping.


 We removed mid-line attacks from the game's main mechanic, parrying. We initially added this attack style to keep things straightforward, but we realized it caused confusion. Now, you only need to parry attacks from the left or right.


 Improvements were made to enhance the feel of parrying and perfect blocking.


 We've fixed many minor bugs related to the game.

The Carnival of Company is better today than it was yesterday, and our goal is to make it even better tomorrow.
If you play the demo, please be sure to give us your feedback.

Looking Ahead:

For the next update, our goals include:


 Adding Spanish language support.


 We were a bit reserved in explaining the game's story to avoid losing players' interest, but we’re overcoming that fear now. We will more freely share the rich backstory, increasing the number of dialogues between Marcus and Jack. We’ll also provide continuous hints about what the Carnival really is. Players will have the option to skip these dialogues if they choose.


 We’ll revisit the foliage to better match the theme. Flowers will take on a more demonic look while still remaining visually appealing. After all, if the realms of demons looked too dreadful, even demons wouldn’t want to live there.


 We expect to encounter and fix several bugs.

Until our next descent into terror among the flowers,
Deniz and Abil ❤️❤️❤️

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Improvements and Thanks
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934370/9c477be11125dbc031a106da34f96d13e5c7a5b5.jpg

The Steam Next Fest was very beneficial for us.

 We will explain the game's P.O.C system and parry system more clearly. 
 We will reveal the reason why Jack eats the flesh of his enemies earlier in the game.
 We will also make improvements to the UI.
 We will adjust the abundance of money and the reward mechanics in the demo.

We hope to release the game in the best possible way.
The new patch will include some additional fixes, so it will take a little more time. (The patch will likely be released in 15 days)
Thank you to everyone who added us to their wishlist and provided feedback.
